unit.why: A Zohar Hadash teaching on self-abasement frames a short first-person memorate by the author: wicked men insulted him, he stayed silent, and R. Asher of Ropshitz remarked on his shining face. It goes on to a homiletic and confessional reflection.
unit.boundary_note: anecdote embedded in a numbered teaching (לז) of a homiletic series; the narrative core is short

stories.end_quote: יש מעט כח ליכנוס וכו' עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: Citing the Zohar on a man who makes himself like dust, the author (R. Yitzhak Isaac of Komarno) recounts how wicked men slandered and insulted him and he barely felt it. When R. Asher of Ropshitz saw his face shining, he explained that God let him taste His sweetness, and he says the persecution brought him great Torah insight.
